free_tier.stated: no free tier. The vendor catalogue lists five GPU plans, every one with in_stock false: Intel Arc Pro A40 $45 a month, NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 $185, RTX PRO 5000 $450, RTX PRO 6000 $885 and B300 $4555. H100, A100 80 GB, L40S, RTX 4090 and L4 are not listed. The price index divides $185 a month by 730 hours to USD 0.25 per GPU-hour for the RTX PRO 4000, which is not a published hourly rate. The vendor GPU page lists bare-metal servers from $1545 a month (8 x RTX Pro 4000) and $1785 a month (2 x RTX PRO 6000). Block storage is USD 4 per TB per month, bandwidth is included on every plan, billing is prepaid monthly with a one-month minimum rental, and cancelling gives no partial refund

egress.terms: 'None of these listed configurations is reported in stock'; and the terms 'Billing is monthly, prepaid', 'Minimum rental time: 1 month; cancelling gives no partial refund', 'Data out: bandwidth included on every plan'

chaining: A USD 185 month with bandwidth included is a fixed-cost way to hold one card continuously, but LeaderGPU's USD 140 month for a 3090 is cheaper and this is a commitment, so it only composes with a workload that runs for most of 730 hours.

limits.value: A one-month prepaid commitment with no partial refund is the binding term: a cancelled month is a lost month, and none of the five GPU plans in the vendor catalogue was in stock on the day checked.
